tldr: From Oct 3 to Oct 17, papers examined retrieval in agents and on-device LLMs under execution constraints: CPU retrieval scheduling, skill routing, tool retrieval, and agent memory. The shared thread was that retrieval is judged by what happens at run time, not only by semantic match.
whats_new: LangChain's Oct 23 post says its Deep Agents harness fixes clumsy searches, oversized results, and stale data to get the right context in, moving the theme from papers to a shipped harness.
why_it_matters: Retrieval for skills, tools, and memory can fail at run time through unavailable tools, latency contention, oversized results, or stale data, so relevance-only scoring is not enough.

status.detail: Four papers frame retrieval as an execution problem; LangChain's Oct 23 post is the first practitioner write-up in the thread.

beats.headline: PhaseGate schedules CPU retrieval around on-device LLM decoding
beats.summary: Concurrent retrieval workers on unified memory raise p95 decode latency.

beats.headline: Skill-router paper optimizes skill injections for retrieval and execution
beats.summary: Covers third-party skills selected dynamically by skill routers.

beats.headline: RATED adds tool availability during execution to tool retrieval
beats.summary: Targets methods that optimize semantic relevance but ignore execution-time availability.

beats.headline: EPGM brings execution provenance to budgeted agent memory retrieval
LangChain applies retrieval techniques in its Deep Agents harness
beats.summary: A practitioner post on search, result size, and stale data.

open_questions: Do any of the papers report results on a public agent benchmark that others can reproduce?
Does any skill router or tool-retrieval library adopt execution-aware scoring?
Does LangChain publish measurements showing how its retrieval changes affect Deep Agents task success or context use?
take_for_builders: Log for each retrieved tool, skill, or memory whether it was available and succeeded at run time, and cap result size, so you can measure the gap these papers and LangChain's post target.
